observations.units: dimensionless; the label states no unit and names the samples a strength relative to the frame mean
observations.meaning: One delay frame of the archive-published SHARAD three-dimensional radargram of eastern Deuteronilus Mensae: every delay sample at projected X index 640 and Y index 710. The bundle readme calls the .dat member a table of binary data and the PDS3 label counts it in 14,400-byte fixed-length records, so this frame is record 909,511 of 1,817,600. The pinned PDS4 label owns the grid, sampling, scalar type, projection and statistics.
observations.citation: Putzig, N., F. Foss, M. Perry, G. Morgan, and P. Sava (2025). Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter SHARAD 3D Radargram Bundle. PDS Geosciences (GEO) Node. https://doi.org/10.17189/a5av-yc11
limitations: This is one pinned byte range of a 26,173,440,000-byte archive member, not the whole volume. The range is the one the label's axis arithmetic places at these indices, and the reader refuses a read outside it.
Delay time is the archive's vertical coordinate, referenced to the areoid plus 10.125 km. The bundle supplies no dielectric model or datum for a metric depth, so no depth conversion is qualified.

The samples are backscatter strength, the square root of backscatter power, relative to the frame mean. They are not ice fraction, density, composition, or a material boundary, and brightness alone does not establish a geologic reflector.

The volume is an archive-published reconstruction from 466 SHARAD observations over MRO orbits 3081 through 64793, not a direct measurement at each cell, so return localization depends on that reconstruction.
The observation interval is the whole product's, spanning every contributing track; it is not the time of this frame.

The label's 475 m grid spacing and 0.0375 microsecond delay interval are sampling intervals. Achieved resolution is not supplied here; the bundle's 3d_processing_v2.0.pdf user guide documents the processing parameters.
The archive publishes no checksum for the whole member. The pin covers exactly these bytes, and the acquisition accepts only a 206 Partial Content answer over exactly this range.
The release notes' known imaging artifacts are ground tracks in the Planum Australe version 1 volume, not in this product.

In this label the PDS4 cartography and the array axes are transposed: the upper-left corner x of -337012.5 m equals the array Y start and the upper-left corner y of 303762.5 m is the negated array X start. The reader uses the array axes only, and no geographic position is derived from the cartography here.
No product descriptor is published for this slice yet: the shared F16 descriptor route inspects a FITS array through Astropy, which this native PDS4 member is not.

observations.meaning: The constant-X radargram plane at projected X index 640 of the same volume: the 1,420 consecutive delay frames that the label's last-index-fastest order makes one contiguous byte range, 20,448,000 bytes covering every Y and delay sample at that X. The delay frame pinned beside it is the sub-range of this plane at Y index 710.
